content: 1. Administer 500 mg of Penicillin V potassium orally every 12 hours, or 250 mg orally every 6 hours, for a duration of 10 days. 2. For mild infections, administer 2–4 grams per day orally, divided into doses every 6 hours, for 8 weeks. 3. For surgical prophylaxis, administer 2–4 grams per day orally, divided into doses every 6 hours, for 6–12 months. 4. For children under 5 years of age, administer 125 mg orally every 12 hours. For children over 5 years, administer 250 mg orally every 12 hours. 5. For children, administer 250 mg orally every 8–12 hours for 10 days. 6. For adolescents, administer 250 mg orally every 6 hours or 500 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days. 7. For primary prevention in children under 5 years, administer 125 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days. For children over 5 years, administer 250 mg orally every 12 hours for 10 days. 8. For prophylaxis in children, administer 125–250 mg orally every 12 hours on a continuous basis. 9. Penicillin V potassium should be taken on an empty stomach. 10. Monitor renal and hematologic systems during treatment. 11. Penicillin V potassium decreases the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic treatment is completed. 12. Avoid coadministration of cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as antibiotics may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 13. Demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, omadacycline, sarecycline, and tetracyclines in general may reduce the bactericidal effects of penicillin V potassium due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillin V potassium if used concomitantly with tetracyclines. 15. Penicillin V potassium decreases the efficacy of microbiota oral supplements containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 16. Penicillin V potassium decreases the efficacy of live vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic treatment is completed. 17. Penicillin V potassium increases the toxicity of amifampridine, which can cause seizures. Coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. Penicillin V potassium decreases the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors, such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab, through unspecified interaction mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Penicillin V potassium decreases the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Penicillin V potassium decreases the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, such as dienogest/estradiol valerate, ethinylestradiol, and levonorgestrel/ethinylestradiol/ferrous bisglycinate, by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternate or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 21. Penicillin V potassium increases the levels of ibuprofen (IV), methyclothiazide, sodium phenylacetate, and rose hips by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Penicillin V potassium increases the levels of aspirin, aspirin rectal, and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by decreasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Penicillin V potassium increases the levels of furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, and chlorothiazide by decreasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Probenecid increases the levels of penicillin V potassium by competing for renal tubular clearance. Monitor closely. 25. Neomycin (oral) decreases the levels of penicillin V potassium by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Azithromycin, clarithromycin, erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate), and chloramphenicol decrease the efficacy of penicillin V potassium due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of these interactions is unknown. 27. Penicillin V potassium and choline magnesium trisalicylate may increase each other’s levels due to plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Penicillin V potassium and salicylates (non-ASA) or salsalate may increase each other’s levels due to plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Penicillin V potassium and willow bark may increase each other’s levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely.
